title: Seeking Help Through Patience and Prayer
summary: God is with the steadfast. Reflections on patience in loss and hardship, the ease that comes with difficulty, and patience as a gift that can be grown.

sections.heading: Patience joined with prayer
paragraphs: The Qur'an addresses believers with a simple instruction for hard times: seek help in steadfastness and prayer, for God is with the steadfast [Q 2:153].

Patience is not presented as a lonely effort of willpower. It is joined with prayer, a turning toward God. And the promise attached is not only reward later but companionship now: God is with those who are steadfast.

sections.heading: Tests, and a sentence to hold
paragraphs: The verses that follow are honest about life. They say that people will be tried with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth, lives and crops, and then they give glad tidings to the steadfast [Q 2:155].

They describe the steadfast as those who, when a misfortune strikes them, say that we belong to God and to Him we are returning [Q 2:156]. Many Muslims say these words when they hear of a death or a loss.
The sentence does not deny pain. It places pain inside a larger truth: what we have is entrusted to us, and our lives are moving toward God. That perspective can steady a heart that feels shaken.

sections.heading: With hardship comes ease
paragraphs: A short chapter of the Qur'an offers a reassurance: with hardship goes ease [Q 94:5]. The words come with hardship, not only after it, and many readers take comfort in the thought that relief may be near even inside difficulty.
Many people find in this a reason to look for small mercies in hard seasons: a friend who called, a moment of calm, a door that opened unexpectedly. Noticing them is part of patience.

The reassurance is then repeated in the very next verse [Q 94:6]. Repetition in speech is often a way of comforting someone who needs to hear a thing twice. In moments of strain, many of us are exactly that person.

sections.heading: Patience at the first shock
paragraphs: The Prophet (peace be upon him) once passed a woman weeping beside a grave and told her to fear God and be patient. Not recognising him, she told him to go away, saying he had not been struck by a calamity like hers [H bukhari 1283].
When she learned who he was, she went to his house and told him she had not recognised him. He did not rebuke her, but said that patience is at the first stroke of a calamity [H bukhari 1283].
The story is full of gentleness. Her grief was real, and his response did not shame her. Yet it teaches that the moment of first impact, when we are most raw, is where patience matters most.

sections.heading: The best of gifts
paragraphs: In another narration, after giving to people who asked him again and again until nothing was left, the Prophet said that whoever remains patient, God will make him patient, and that no one is given a blessing better and greater than patience [H bukhari 1469].
This is deeply encouraging. Patience is not a fixed trait that some people simply have. It can be grown through effort, and God helps the one who tries.

Patience also includes self-control in anger. The Prophet said that the strong person is not the one who overcomes people by his strength, but the one who controls himself while angry [H bukhari 6114]. Real strength is often quiet.

We might take a few steps from these texts this week: turning to prayer when pressure rises [Q 2:153], saying the words of return in moments of loss [Q 2:156], pausing before reacting in anger [H bukhari 6114], and asking God for the gift of patience itself [H bukhari 1469].

ayahs.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
ayahs.english: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast

ayahs.arabic: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
ayahs.english: And surely We shall try you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and crops; but give glad tidings to the steadfast

ayahs.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
ayahs.english: Who say, when a misfortune striketh them: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning

ayahs.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرًا
ayahs.english: But lo! with hardship goeth ease

ayahs.arabic: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرࣰ ا
ayahs.english: Lo! with hardship goeth ease

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، حَدَّثَنَا ثَابِتٌ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ مَرَّ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِامْرَأَةٍ تَبْكِي عِنْدَ قَبْرٍ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اتَّقِي اللَّهَ وَاصْبِرِي ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَتْ إِلَيْكَ عَنِّي، فَإِنَّكَ لَمْ تُصَبْ بِمُصِيبَتِي، وَلَمْ تَعْرِفْهُ‏.‏ فَقِيلَ لَهَا إِنَّهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَأَتَتْ باب النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلَمْ تَجِدْ عِنْدَهُ بَوَّابِينَ فَقَالَتْ لَمْ أَعْرِفْكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا الصَّبْرُ عِنْدَ الصَّدْمَةِ الأُولَى ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Anas bin Malik:The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a woman who was weeping beside a grave. He told her to fear Allah and be patient. She said to him, "Go away, for you have not been afflicted with a calamity like mine." And she did not recognize him. Then she was informed that he was the Prophet (ﷺ) . so she went to the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and there she did not find any guard. Then she said to him, "I did not recognize you." He said, "Verily, the patience is at the first stroke of a calamity

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ اللَّيْثِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ نَاسًا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ سَأَلُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَعْطَاهُمْ، ثُمَّ سَأَلُوهُ فَأَعْطَاهُمْ، حَتَّى نَفِدَ مَا عِنْدَهُ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ مَا يَكُونُ عِنْدِي مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ أَدَّخِرَهُ عَنْكُمْ، وَمَنْ يَسْتَعْفِفْ يُعِفَّهُ اللَّهُ، وَمَنْ يَسْتَغْنِ يُغْنِهِ اللَّهُ، وَمَنْ يَتَصَبَّرْ يُصَبِّرْهُ اللَّهُ، وَمَا أُعْطِيَ أَحَدٌ عَطَاءً خَيْرًا وَأَوْسَعَ مِنَ الصَّبْرِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri:Some Ansari persons asked for (something) from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he gave them. They again asked him for (something) and he again gave them. And then they asked him and he gave them again till all that was with him finished. And then he said "If I had anything. I would not keep it away from you. (Remember) Whoever abstains from asking others, Allah will make him contented, and whoever tries to make himself self-sufficient, Allah will make him self-sufficient. And whoever remains patient, Allah will make him patient. Nobody can be given a blessing better and greater than patience

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The strong is not the one who overcomes the people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger

title: Charity That Grows: Giving With a Sincere Heart
summary: A grain that grows seven ears, a kind word better than hurtful giving, and charity in every good deed: reflections on giving with sincerity and respect.

sections.heading: A grain of seven ears
paragraphs: The Qur'an describes those who spend their wealth in the way of God with a striking image: a single grain that grows seven ears, with a hundred grains in every ear, and God gives increase manifold to whom He wills [Q 2:261].
The image is about growth we cannot see. A gift given quietly may seem small in the moment, yet its effect, in the life of the receiver and in the giver's own heart, can be far larger than its size.

sections.heading: Without reproach
paragraphs: The Qur'an states that a kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury [Q 2:263]. Charity is not only about what leaves our hands. It is also about how the other person is left feeling.
This protects the dignity of those who receive. It reminds givers that they are not owed gratitude or control, and that a gift used to humiliate has lost its spirit.
The verse closes by describing God as Absolute and Clement [Q 2:263]. He does not need our giving; we are the ones who need the good it does to us and to others.

sections.heading: For the sake of God alone
paragraphs: The Qur'an praises those who feed the needy, the orphan and the prisoner for love of God [Q 76:8], saying that they feed only for His sake and wish for no reward or thanks from those they help [Q 76:9].
Sincerity frees the giver. If we are not waiting for thanks, we cannot be disappointed when it does not come, and our giving does not depend on the reactions of others.

sections.heading: Even half a date
paragraphs: The Prophet (peace be upon him) told people to save themselves from the Fire even by giving half a date in charity [H bukhari 1417]. No gift is too small to count.
This is a gentle encouragement for anyone who feels they have little. The worth of charity is not measured only by amount. A small gift given sincerely has its own value before God.

It also guards against a quiet kind of delay. Many people wait until they can give something large, and in waiting give nothing. Half a date is a reminder that the right time to begin is now, with whatever is in our hands.

sections.heading: Charity in every good deed
paragraphs: The Prophet also widened the meaning of charity far beyond money. He said that charity is due for every joint of the body on every day the sun rises, and gave examples: judging justly between two people, helping someone onto his riding animal or lifting his luggage onto it, a good word, every step taken toward prayer, and removing something harmful from the way [H bukhari 2989].

In another very short narration, he said that enjoining all that is good is charity [H bukhari 6021]. These teachings open the door to everyone. A person with no spare money still has words, time, strength and attention to give.

Perhaps this week we might notice the charities already within reach: a fair word in a dispute, help with a neighbour's bags, a kind message to someone who is struggling, or clearing an obstacle from a path [H bukhari 2989].
Charity in these texts is generous, quiet, respectful and sincere. It grows like a seed [Q 2:261], it guards the dignity of others [Q 2:263], and it is open to every person, whatever they hold.

ayahs.arabic: مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنۢبَتَتۡ سَبۡعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةࣲ مِّاْئَةُ حَبَّةࣲۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُضَٰعِفُ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
ayahs.english: The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

ayahs.arabic: ۞قَوۡلࣱ مَّعۡرُوفࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةٌ خَيۡرࣱ مِّن صَدَقَةࣲ يَتۡبَعُهَآ أَذࣰ ىۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمࣱ‏
ayahs.english: A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement

ayahs.arabic: وَيُطۡعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ مِسۡكِينࣰ ا وَيَتِيمࣰ ا وَأَسِيرًا
ayahs.english: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him

ayahs.arabic: إِنَّمَا نُطۡعِمُكُمۡ لِوَجۡهِ ٱللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ وَلَا شُكُورًا
ayahs.english: (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَعْقِلٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَدِيَّ بْنَ حَاتِمٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated `Adi bin Hatim heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying:"Save yourself from Hell-fire even by giving half a date-fruit in charity

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْحَاقُ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ هَمَّامٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ كُلُّ سُلاَمَى مِنَ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ، يَعْدِلُ بَيْنَ الاِثْنَيْنِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَيُعِينُ الرَّجُلَ عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ، فَيَحْمِلُ عَلَيْهَا، أَوْ يَرْفَعُ عَلَيْهَا مَتَاعَهُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَكُلُّ خَطْوَةٍ يَخْطُوهَا إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَيُمِيطُ الأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ صَدَقَةٌ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "There is a (compulsory) Sadaqa (charity) to be given for every joint of the human body (as a sign of gratitude to Allah) everyday the sun rises. To judge justly between two persons is regarded as Sadaqa, and to help a man concerning his riding animal by helping him to ride it or by lifting his luggage on to it, is also regarded as Sadaqa, and (saying) a good word is also Sadaqa, and every step taken on one's way to offer the compulsory prayer (in the mosque) is also Sadaqa and to remove a harmful thing from the way is also Sadaqa
hadiths.section: Fighting for the Cause of Allah (Jihaad)

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَيَّاشٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو غَسَّانَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ كُلُّ مَعْرُوفٍ صَدَقَةٌ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Jabir bin `Abdullah:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, Enjoining, all that is good is a Sadaqa

title: Love, Mercy and Kindness in the Family
summary: Love and mercy between spouses, gentleness with parents, and keeping ties with relatives: what the Qur'an and hadith teach about family life.

sections.heading: Rest, love and mercy
paragraphs: The Qur'an counts marriage among the signs of God. It says that He created for people spouses from among themselves so that they might find rest in them, and ordained between them love and mercy [Q 30:21].

Love and mercy are named together. Love may be strongest in easy times; mercy carries a family through illness, mistakes and the tiredness of ordinary days. The verse closes by saying that there are signs in this for people who reflect [Q 30:21].

sections.heading: Gentleness with parents
paragraphs: One passage links kindness to parents directly with the worship of God alone [Q 17:23]. It speaks of parents in old age and asks that we not even say a word of irritation to them, nor repulse them, but speak to them a gracious word [Q 17:23].
It continues with a tender image: lowering to them the wing of submission out of mercy, and praying for God to have mercy on them as they cared for us when we were little [Q 17:24].

Care for ageing parents can be demanding, and few of us do it perfectly. These verses do not pretend otherwise. They point to our tone, our patience and our prayers as places where kindness can grow even when we feel stretched.
The Qur'an also recalls what mothers carry, describing a mother bearing her child in weakness upon weakness, and asking people to give thanks to God and to their parents [Q 31:14].

sections.heading: Your mother, then your mother
paragraphs: A man once asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) who was most entitled to his good companionship. He answered, your mother. The man asked who came next, and he said again, your mother, and a third time, your mother, and then, your father [H bukhari 5971].
The repetition is memorable. It asks us to notice the people whose care for us may be the least visible, and to answer it with attention, time and warmth.

It also sits naturally beside the verse about a mother's weakness upon weakness [Q 31:14]. The Qur'an names the burden, and the narration names the response. Neither erases the place of the father, who is mentioned in both, but both invite special gratitude toward mothers.

sections.heading: Keeping ties
paragraphs: The Prophet also said that whoever would love to be given more provision and a longer life should keep good relations with his relatives [H bukhari 5986]. Family relationships are presented as a source of blessing, not only of duty.

Keeping ties today might mean a regular call to an aunt, a visit to a cousin we have drifted from, or a first step toward healing an old disagreement. Small, steady contact often matters more than grand gestures.

sections.heading: Best to one's own
paragraphs: In another narration, the Prophet said that the best of people is the one who is best to his wife, and that he was the best of them to his own wives [H ibnmajah 1977]. Goodness is measured not only in public but in how we treat those closest to us.

It can be easier to be patient with strangers than with family, because at home we feel we can let our guard down. These texts gently turn that around: home is the first place where character is seen.

Love and mercy [Q 30:21], gracious words to parents [Q 17:23], gratitude [Q 31:14] and steady ties with relatives are not separate projects. Together they describe a home where faith is lived. We can ask God to help us build that, one ordinary day at a time.

ayahs.arabic: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
ayahs.english: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

ayahs.arabic: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
ayahs.english: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little

ayahs.arabic: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا لِّتَسۡكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
ayahs.english: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect

ayahs.arabic: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهۡنًا عَلَىٰ وَهۡنࣲ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ فِي عَامَيۡنِ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيۡكَ إِلَيَّ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
ayahs.english: And We have enjoined upon man concerning his partners - His mother beareth him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years - Give thanks unto Me and unto thy parents. Unto Me is the journeying

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ الْقَعْقَاعِ بْنِ شُبْرُمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي زُرْعَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَنْ أَحَقُّ بِحُسْنِ صَحَابَتِي قَالَ ‏"‏ أُمُّكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ مَنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ أُمُّكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ مَنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ أُمُّكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ مَنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ ثُمَّ أَبُوكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَقَالَ ابْنُ شُبْرُمَةَ وَيَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو زُرْعَةَ مِثْلَهُ‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Huraira:A man came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Who is more entitled to be treated with the best companionship by me?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Your mother." The man said. "Who is next?" The Prophet said, "Your mother." The man further said, "Who is next?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Your mother." The man asked for the fourth time, "Who is next?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Your father

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا اللَّيْثُ، عَنْ عُقَيْلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَيُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Anas bin Malik:Allah's Apostle said, "Whoever loves that he be granted more wealth and that his lease of life be prolonged then he should keep good relations with his Kith and kin

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بِشْرٍ، بَكْرُ بْنُ خَلَفٍ وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ ثَوْبَانَ، عَنْ عَمِّهِ، عُمَارَةَ بْنِ ثَوْبَانَ عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ ‏ "‏ خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لأَهْلِهِ وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لأَهْلِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏
hadiths.english: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that:the Prophet said: "The best of you is the one who is best to his wife, and I am the best of you to my wives

title: My Lord, Increase Me in Knowledge
summary: A prayer for more knowledge, the gift of the pen, and the Prophet's parable of rain on different ground: reflections on learning and teaching.

sections.heading: A prayer for more
paragraphs: Among the prayers the Qur'an teaches is a short one: My Lord, increase me in knowledge [Q 20:114]. It was addressed to the Prophet (peace be upon him) himself, which tells us that learning is never finished, whoever we are.
The prayer is humble. It assumes that we do not yet know enough, and that knowledge is a gift we ask for, not only a prize we win by effort. Asking and striving belong together.

sections.heading: Taught what we did not know
paragraphs: The Qur'an describes God as the One who teaches the human being what he did not know [Q 96:5]. Understanding is presented as part of God's generosity to people, not something we produce on our own.

This gives dignity to every honest act of learning: a child tracing letters, a student working through a hard text, an adult returning to study after many years. Each is receiving something that God has made possible.

The same passage speaks of God who teaches by the pen [Q 96:4], and opens with the command to read in the name of the Lord who creates [Q 96:1]. Reading, writing and recording knowledge are placed at the very beginning, joined to the remembrance of God.

sections.heading: Not the same
paragraphs: One verse asks a simple question: are those who know equal with those who do not? It adds that only people of understanding pay heed [Q 39:9]. The question follows the picture of someone who worships through the night, mindful of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [Q 39:9].
Knowledge here is not only information. It is awareness that shapes how a person lives. The verse links knowing with devotion, attentiveness and hope.

Elsewhere the Qur'an says that God will exalt those who believe and those who have knowledge to high ranks [Q 58:11]. The same verse speaks about making room for others in gatherings, a reminder that learning and good manners are meant to go together.

sections.heading: Rain on different ground
paragraphs: The Prophet compared the guidance and knowledge he brought to abundant rain falling on different kinds of land [H bukhari 79]. Some ground was fertile and brought forth plants. Some was hard and held the water so that people could drink and farm. Some was barren and gave no benefit.

He explained that the first is like the person who understands the religion, benefits from it, learns and then teaches others, and the last is like the person who pays no attention to the guidance [H bukhari 79]. The image asks each of us what kind of ground we are.

It also offers encouragement to those who do not see themselves as scholars. Holding knowledge so that others can benefit, by supporting teachers, sharing good resources or passing on accurately what we have learned, has its own place in the picture.

sections.heading: Learning and teaching
paragraphs: In another narration, the Prophet said that when God wants good for a person, He gives him understanding of the religion. He described himself as a distributor, while the giving comes from God [H bukhari 71].
He also said that the best among people are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it [H bukhari 5027]. Learning is completed in sharing, and teaching is itself a way of learning more deeply.
Taken together, these narrations describe knowledge as something received, understood and then passed on. None of these stages is complete alone.

These texts suggest a modest plan: ask God regularly for more knowledge [Q 20:114], set aside some time each week to study, check what we read against reliable sources, and pass on what benefits others. Knowledge then becomes a form of worship and service at once.

ayahs.arabic: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يُقۡضَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهُۥۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدۡنِي عِلۡمࣰ ا
ayahs.english: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge

ayahs.arabic: أَمَّنۡ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ سَاجِدࣰ ا وَقَآئِمࣰ ا يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرۡجُواْ رَحۡمَةَ رَبِّهِۦۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
ayahs.english: Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever)? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Are those who know equal with those who know not? But only men of understanding will pay heed

ayahs.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمۡ تَفَسَّحُواْ فِي ٱلۡمَجَٰلِسِ فَٱفۡسَحُواْ يَفۡسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُواْ فَٱنشُزُواْ يَرۡفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ دَرَجَٰتࣲۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
ayahs.english: O ye who believe! when it is said unto you, Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter). And when it is said, Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is Informed of what ye do

ayahs.arabic: ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ
ayahs.english: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth

ayahs.arabic: ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِٱلۡقَلَمِ
ayahs.english: Who teacheth by the pen

ayahs.arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مَا لَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ
ayahs.english: Teacheth man that which he knew not

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ أُسَامَةَ، عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي بُرْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَثَلُ مَا بَعَثَنِي اللَّهُ بِهِ مِنَ الْهُدَى وَالْعِلْمِ كَمَثَلِ الْغَيْثِ الْكَثِيرِ أَصَابَ أَرْضًا، فَكَانَ مِنْهَا نَقِيَّةٌ قَبِلَتِ الْمَاءَ، فَأَنْبَتَتِ الْكَلأَ وَالْعُشْبَ الْكَثِيرَ، وَكَانَتْ مِنْهَا أَجَادِبُ أَمْسَكَتِ الْمَاءَ، فَنَفَعَ اللَّهُ بِهَا النَّاسَ، فَشَرِبُوا وَسَقَوْا وَزَرَعُوا، وَأَصَابَتْ مِنْهَا طَائِفَةً أُخْرَى، إِنَّمَا هِيَ قِيعَانٌ لاَ تُمْسِكُ مَاءً، وَلاَ تُنْبِتُ كَلأً، فَذَلِكَ مَثَلُ مَنْ فَقِهَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ وَنَفَعَهُ مَا بَعَثَنِي اللَّهُ بِهِ، فَعَلِمَ وَعَلَّمَ، وَمَثَلُ مَنْ لَمْ يَرْفَعْ بِذَلِكَ رَأْسًا، وَلَمْ يَقْبَلْ هُدَى اللَّهِ الَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ وَكَانَ مِنْهَا طَائِفَةٌ قَيَّلَتِ الْمَاءَ‏.‏ قَاعٌ يَعْلُوهُ الْمَاءُ، وَالصَّفْصَفُ الْمُسْتَوِي مِنَ الأَرْضِ‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Musa:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The example of guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain falling on the earth, some of which was fertile soil that absorbed rain water and brought forth vegetation and grass in abundance. (And) another portion of it was hard and held the rain water and Allah benefited the people with it and they utilized it for drinking, making their animals drink from it and for irrigation of the land for cultivation. (And) a portion of it was barren which could neither hold the water nor bring forth vegetation (then that land gave no benefits). The first is the example of the person who comprehends Allah's religion and gets benefit (from the knowledge) which Allah has revealed through me (the Prophet) and learns and then teaches others. The last example is that of a person who does not care for it and does not take Allah's guidance revealed through me (He is like that barren land)

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ عُفَيْرٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ قَالَ حُمَيْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ سَمِعْتُ مُعَاوِيَةَ، خَطِيبًا يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ، وَإِنَّمَا أَنَا قَاسِمٌ وَاللَّهُ يُعْطِي، وَلَنْ تَزَالَ هَذِهِ الأُمَّةُ قَائِمَةً عَلَى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ لاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ مَنْ خَالَفَهُمْ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Muawiya:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If Allah wants to do good to a person, He makes him comprehend the religion. I am just a distributor, but the grant is from Allah. (And remember) that this nation (true Muslims) will keep on following Allah's teachings strictly and they will not be harmed by any one going on a different path till Allah's order (Day of Judgment) is established

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مِنْهَالٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي عَلْقَمَةُ بْنُ مَرْثَدٍ، سَمِعْتُ سَعْدَ بْنَ عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ السُّلَمِيِّ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَقْرَأَ أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ فِي إِمْرَةِ عُثْمَانَ حَتَّى كَانَ الْحَجَّاجُ، قَالَ وَذَاكَ الَّذِي أَقْعَدَنِي مَقْعَدِي هَذَا‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated `Uthman:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The best among you (Muslims) are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it

title: Standing Firm for Justice, Even Against Ourselves
summary: The Qur'an asks for justice even against ourselves and toward those we dislike. Reflections on fairness, kindness and equality before the law.

sections.heading: Justice begins with ourselves
paragraphs: The Qur'an asks believers to be staunch in justice as witnesses for God, even if it is against themselves, their parents or their relatives, and whether the person concerned is rich or poor [Q 4:135].

This is a demanding standard. It is natural to lean toward ourselves and the people we love. The verse names that pull directly and asks us not to follow passion in a way that turns us from the truth [Q 4:135].
It also removes another kind of bias: favouring the wealthy because of their influence, or the poor out of misplaced sympathy. God, the verse reminds us, is nearer to both than we are [Q 4:135].

sections.heading: Justice toward those we dislike
paragraphs: A second verse turns to the opposite temptation. It asks believers to be steadfast witnesses in equity, and not to let hatred of any people lead them away from dealing justly; justice, it says, is nearer to piety [Q 5:8].

Fairness toward friends is relatively easy. Fairness toward people who have hurt us, or whose views we oppose, is the real test. The Qur'an treats this kind of justice as nearness to duty before God, not as a concession.
In a time of fierce disagreements, online and offline, this verse offers a quiet discipline: describe others accurately, judge actions on evidence, and refuse to let anger write the verdict.

sections.heading: Justice joined with kindness
paragraphs: Another verse places justice beside kindness and giving to relatives, and sets them against lewdness, abomination and wickedness [Q 16:90]. Justice in the Qur'an is not cold. It travels together with good treatment of people.
This pairing helps us. Justice keeps kindness honest, and kindness keeps justice humane. A community that has only one of them will struggle.

The verse ends by saying that God exhorts people so that they may take heed [Q 16:90]. It is offered as counsel to reflect on, a reminder that fairness and kindness are meant to shape our daily choices: how we divide work, settle disputes, review a colleague, or speak about a rival.

sections.heading: Helping the oppressor
paragraphs: The Prophet (peace be upon him) once told his companions to help their brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. They understood how to help someone who is wronged, but asked how one helps a wrongdoer. He answered: by preventing him from oppressing others [H bukhari 2444].

This turns loyalty on its head. True support for a friend who is doing wrong is not to defend him, but to hold him back. Sometimes the most caring words we can say are the ones that stop a wrong from continuing.

sections.heading: No one above the law
paragraphs: A well-known narration describes a time when a woman from the clan of Bani Makhzum committed theft, and the people of Quraish, worried about her, looked for someone to intercede for her. When Usama bin Zaid spoke to the Prophet on her behalf, he objected to intercession in such a matter and then addressed the people [H bukhari 3475].

He told them that earlier nations were destroyed because when a noble person among them did wrong they let him go, while when a poor person did the same they held him to account. He then said that even his own daughter Fatima would not be spared [H bukhari 3475].

The heart of the lesson is equality before justice. Rank, family and connections should not change the outcome. That principle speaks to courts and governments, but also to workplaces, schools and families, wherever rules are applied to some and excused for others.

Justice, as these texts present it, starts with honesty about ourselves, extends even to those we dislike, walks with kindness, restrains our friends when they do wrong, and applies to everyone alike. It is a lifelong practice, and one we can ask God to help us keep [Q 4:135].

ayahs.arabic: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
ayahs.english: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

ayahs.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
ayahs.english: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

ayahs.arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآيِٕ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَيَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱلۡبَغۡيِۚ يَعِظُكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
ayahs.english: Lo! Allah enjoineth justice and kindness, and giving to kinsfolk, and forbiddeth lewdness and abomination and wickedness. He exhorteth you in order that ye may take heed

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا مُعْتَمِرٌ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ انْصُرْ أَخَاكَ ظَالِمًا أَوْ مَظْلُومًا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَذَا نَنْصُرُهُ مَظْلُومًا، فَكَيْفَ نَنْصُرُهُ ظَالِمًا قَالَ ‏"‏ تَأْخُذُ فَوْقَ يَدَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Anas:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or he is an oppressed one. People asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! It is all right to help him if he is oppressed, but how should we help him if he is an oppressor?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "By preventing him from oppressing others

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا لَيْثٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها أَنَّ قُرَيْشًا، أَهَمَّهُمْ شَأْنُ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمَخْزُومِيَّةِ الَّتِي سَرَقَتْ، فَقَالَ وَمَنْ يُكَلِّمُ فِيهَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالُوا وَمَنْ يَجْتَرِئُ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، حِبُّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَكَلَّمَهُ أُسَامَةُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَتَشْفَعُ فِي حَدٍّ مِنْ حُدُودِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَاخْتَطَبَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا أَهْلَكَ الَّذِينَ قَبْلَكُمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا إِذَا سَرَقَ فِيهِمُ الشَّرِيفُ تَرَكُوهُ، وَإِذَا سَرَقَ فِيهِمُ الضَّعِيفُ أَقَامُوا عَلَيْهِ الْحَدَّ، وَايْمُ اللَّهِ، لَوْ أَنَّ فَاطِمَةَ ابْنَةَ مُحَمَّدٍ سَرَقَتْ لَقَطَعْتُ يَدَهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated `Aisha:The people of Quraish worried about the lady from Bani Makhzum who had committed theft. They asked, "Who will intercede for her with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" Some said, "No one dare to do so except Usama bin Zaid the beloved one to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ." When Usama spoke about that to Allah's Apostle Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, (to him), "Do you try to intercede for somebody in a case connected with Allah's Prescribed Punishments?" Then he got up and delivered a sermon saying, "What destroyed the nations preceding you, was that if a noble amongst them stole, they would forgive him, and if a poor person amongst them stole, they would inflict Allah's Legal punishment on him. By Allah, if Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would cut off her hand

title: Mercy That Embraces All Things
summary: The Prophet was sent as a mercy, and God's mercy embraces all things. Reflections on receiving that mercy without despair and showing it to others.

sections.heading: Mercy as the setting of the message
paragraphs: The Qur'an describes the mission of the Prophet (peace be upon him) in a single phrase: he was sent only as a mercy for the peoples [Q 21:107]. Mercy is not one teaching among many; it is the frame in which the message arrives.
This shapes how we read everything else. Commands, warnings and stories all sit within a purpose of mercy, and those who follow the message are invited to carry that mercy into the world.

sections.heading: Wider than our mistakes
paragraphs: In one verse God says that His mercy embraces all things [Q 7:156]. Nothing in creation lies outside its reach. The same verse speaks of those for whom it will be written: people who guard against evil, give the poor-due and believe in God's revelations [Q 7:156].
There is hope and responsibility together here. Mercy is vast, and we are invited to turn toward it through the way we live.

Another verse speaks directly to people who have wronged themselves, telling them not to despair of God's mercy, for He forgives all sins and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful [Q 39:53]. It is addressed to those who feel furthest away.
Many people carry a quiet belief that they have gone too far to come back. This verse answers that belief gently and firmly. Despair is not the right response to failure; turning back is.

sections.heading: One part out of a hundred
paragraphs: The Prophet described God's mercy through an image of scale. God divided mercy into one hundred parts, kept ninety-nine with Himself and sent one part down to the earth [H bukhari 6000].

Because of that single part, the narration says, His creatures are merciful to one another, so that even a mare lifts its hoof away from its young so as not to tread on it [H bukhari 6000]. Every tender act we witness, in people or in animals, is a trace of that one part.
If one part fills the world with so much care, the narration invites us to imagine what remains with God. That is a thought worth holding on to in hard moments.

sections.heading: Mercy in the home
paragraphs: Mercy is also something we are asked to practise. When the Prophet kissed the young son of Ali, a man sitting nearby said that he had ten children and had never kissed any of them. The Prophet looked at him and said that whoever is not merciful to others will not be treated mercifully [H bukhari 5997].

The lesson came in a small, domestic moment. Affection toward children was not treated as something to be embarrassed about but as mercy. Gentleness at home is part of faith, not a distraction from it.

sections.heading: Mercy received and given
paragraphs: Another narration ties the two directions together. The Compassionate One has mercy on those who are merciful; if we show mercy to those on the earth, the One in the heaven will show mercy to us [H abudawud 4941].

This invites a simple practice. When we ask God for mercy, we can also ask ourselves to whom we have been merciful today: a child, an elderly parent, a tired colleague, an animal, or someone who wronged us.

God's mercy embraces all things [Q 7:156]. We will never match it, but we can reflect it, a little at a time, in the way we speak, forgive and care. That is how a message sent as a mercy continues to reach people [Q 21:107].

Mercy toward ourselves belongs here too. The invitation not to despair [Q 39:53] is also an invitation to stop speaking to ourselves with harshness after a failure, and to return instead with hope. A heart that has felt God's mercy is often better able to show it to others.

ayahs.arabic: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
ayahs.english: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

ayahs.arabic: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
ayahs.english: We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples

ayahs.arabic: ۞قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
ayahs.english: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَكَمُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَخْبَرَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ الْمُسَيَّبِ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الرَّحْمَةَ مِائَةَ جُزْءٍ، فَأَمْسَكَ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ جُزْءًا، وَأَنْزَلَ فِي الأَرْضِ جُزْءًا وَاحِدًا، فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْجُزْءِ يَتَرَاحَمُ الْخَلْقُ، حَتَّى تَرْفَعَ الْفَرَسُ حَافِرَهَا عَنْ وَلَدِهَا خَشْيَةَ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Huraira:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, Allah divided Mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety nine parts with Him and sent down one part to the earth, and because of that, its one single part, His Creations are merciful to each other, so that even the mare lifts up its hoofs away from its baby animal, lest it should trample on it

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْحَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ وَعِنْدَهُ الأَقْرَعُ بْنُ حَابِسٍ التَّمِيمِيُّ جَالِسًا‏.‏ فَقَالَ الأَقْرَعُ إِنَّ لِي عَشَرَةً مِنَ الْوَلَدِ مَا قَبَّلْتُ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا‏.‏ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمُ لاَ يُرْحَمُ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) kissed Al-Hasan bin `Ali while Al-Aqra' bin H`Abis at-Tamim was sitting beside him. Al-Aqra said, "I have ten children and I have never kissed anyone of them," Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) cast a look at him and said, "Whoever is not merciful to others will not be treated mercifully

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَمُسَدَّدٌ، - الْمَعْنَى - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ أَبِي قَابُوسَ، مَوْلًى لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، يَبْلُغُ بِهِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ ارْحَمُوا أَهْلَ الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَقُلْ مُسَدَّدٌ مَوْلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو وَقَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: The Compassionate One has mercy on those who are merciful. If you show mercy to those who are on the earth, He Who is in the heaven will show mercy to you. Musaddad did not say: The client of 'Adb Allah b. 'Amr. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said

title: We Share One Boat: Reflections on Responsible Citizenship
summary: Trusts, cooperation in good, and the Prophet's parable of the ship: what the Qur'an and hadith teach about our responsibility to the people we live among.

sections.heading: Trusts and fairness
paragraphs: Living with others means holding things that are not only ours: shared spaces, public roles, the confidence people place in us. The Qur'an speaks of this when it tells believers to restore trusts to their owners, and to judge justly when judging between people [Q 4:58].

A trust can be a borrowed item, a task we have agreed to do, a position of authority or something told to us in confidence. The verse joins faithfulness in trusts with fairness in judgment, as if to say that a healthy community needs both.
The same verse closes by reminding us that God is Hearer and Seer [Q 4:58]. Responsibility to others is not only a social arrangement; it is lived before God.

sections.heading: Cooperating in good
paragraphs: Another verse gives a simple rule for shared life: help one another to righteousness and piety, and do not help one another to sin and transgression [Q 5:2]. It is a principle that applies to neighbourhoods, workplaces, schools and civic groups alike.

Strikingly, the same verse warns that hatred of a people, even a people who once blocked the believers from the Sacred Mosque, should not lead them to transgress [Q 5:2]. Good citizenship is tested most when we disagree, and when we feel wronged.

Cooperation in good is not limited to people who share our views. It asks whether the work itself is good: caring for the vulnerable, keeping streets safe, supporting honest institutions, and refusing to join in harm.

sections.heading: Everyone is a guardian
paragraphs: The Prophet (peace be upon him) described a whole society as a web of responsibility. All of you are guardians, he said, and each is responsible for what is in his care: the ruler for his people, a man for his family, a woman for her husband's house, and a servant for what he has been entrusted with [H bukhari 893].

No one is left outside this circle. Leaders carry more, but every person holds something in trust. Citizenship begins with taking our own share seriously, rather than waiting for others to take theirs.

sections.heading: The people in the boat
paragraphs: One of the most vivid images in the hadith is of people who drew lots for places on a ship, some on the upper deck and some below. Those below, tired of troubling the others when they went up for water, proposed making a hole in their own part of the ship [H bukhari 2493].

The Prophet explained that if those above let them do it, everyone on board would be destroyed; if they held them back, all would be safe [H bukhari 2493]. A private choice can sink a shared vessel, and silence in the face of harm is not neutral.

The parable fits modern life well. Pollution, corruption, misinformation and neglect of the vulnerable may begin in one corner, but the water rises for everyone. Speaking up kindly and acting early is part of keeping the boat afloat.

sections.heading: The rights of the road
paragraphs: Public space has its own ethics. When the companions said they had no choice but to sit by the roads, the Prophet told them to give the road its rights, and he listed them: lowering the gaze, refraining from harming people, returning greetings, and encouraging good while discouraging evil [H bukhari 2465].

These are small, practical habits. Not obstructing others, not troubling those who pass by, answering a greeting, and gently turning people toward good are all part of being a good neighbour on a shared street.

Responsible citizenship, seen through these texts, is not a grand slogan. It is faithfulness to trusts, cooperation in good, care for our own sphere, the courage to stop harm, and courtesy in public. Each of us can begin today, where we already stand.

ayahs.arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تُؤَدُّواْ ٱلۡأَمَٰنَٰتِ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمۡتُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ أَن تَحۡكُمُواْ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦٓۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعَۢا بَصِيرࣰ ا
ayahs.english: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly. Lo! comely is this which Allah admonisheth you. Lo! Allah is ever Hearer, Seer

ayahs.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُحِلُّواْ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا ٱلشَّهۡرَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ وَلَا ٱلۡهَدۡيَ وَلَا ٱلۡقَلَٰٓئِدَ وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ اۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلۡتُمۡ فَٱصۡطَادُواْۚ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ أَن تَعۡتَدُواْۘ وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
ayahs.english: O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments nor the Sacred Month nor the offerings nor the garlands, nor those repairing to the Sacred House, seeking the grace and pleasure of their Lord. But when ye have left the sacred territory, then go hunting (if ye will). And let not your hatred of a folk who (once) stopped your going to the inviolable place of worship seduce you to transgress; but help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty. Help not one another unto sin and transgression, but keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is severe in punishment

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا يُونُسُ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنَا سَالِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَزَادَ اللَّيْثُ قَالَ يُونُسُ كَتَبَ رُزَيْقُ بْنُ حُكَيْمٍ إِلَى ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ـ وَأَنَا مَعَهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِوَادِي الْقُرَى ـ هَلْ تَرَى أَنْ أُجَمِّعَ‏.‏ وَرُزَيْقٌ عَامِلٌ عَلَى أَرْضٍ يَعْمَلُهَا، وَفِيهَا جَمَاعَةٌ مِنَ السُّودَانِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ، وَرُزَيْقٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَى أَيْلَةَ، فَكَتَبَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ ـ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ ـ يَأْمُرُهُ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ، يُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّ سَالِمًا حَدَّثَهُ أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ، وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، الإِمَامُ رَاعٍ وَمَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، وَالرَّجُلُ رَاعٍ فِي أَهْلِهِ وَهْوَ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، وَالْمَرْأَةُ رَاعِيَةٌ فِي بَيْتِ زَوْجِهَا وَمَسْئُولَةٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهَا، وَالْخَادِمُ رَاعٍ فِي مَالِ سَيِّدِهِ وَمَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ ـ قَالَ وَحَسِبْتُ أَنْ قَدْ قَالَ ـ وَالرَّجُلُ رَاعٍ فِي مَالِ أَبِيهِ وَمَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ وَكُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَمَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Ibn `Umar:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "All of you are Guardians." Yunus said: Ruzaiq bin Hukaim wrote to Ibn Shihab while I was with him at Wadi-al-Qura saying, "Shall I lead the Jumua prayer?" Ruzaiq was working on the land (i.e. farming) and there was a group of Sudanese people and some others with him; Ruzaiq was then the Governor of Aila. Ibn Shihab wrote (to Ruzaiq) ordering him to lead the Jumua prayer and telling him that Salim told him that `Abdullah bin `Umar had said, "I heard Allah's Apostle saying, 'All of you are guardians and responsible for your wards and the things under your care. The Imam (i.e. ruler) is the guardian of his subjects and is responsible for them and a man is the guardian of his family and is responsible for them. A woman is the guardian of her husband's house and is responsible for it. A servant is the guardian of his master's belongings and is responsible for them.' I thought that he also said, 'A man is the guardian of his father's property and is responsible for it. All of you are guardians and responsible for your wards and the things under your care

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَامِرًا، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ النُّعْمَانَ بْنَ بَشِيرٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَثَلُ الْقَائِمِ عَلَى حُدُودِ اللَّهِ وَالْوَاقِعِ فِيهَا كَمَثَلِ قَوْمٍ اسْتَهَمُوا عَلَى سَفِينَةٍ، فَأَصَابَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَعْلاَهَا وَبَعْضُهُمْ أَسْفَلَهَا، فَكَانَ الَّذِينَ فِي أَسْفَلِهَا إِذَا اسْتَقَوْا مِنَ الْمَاءِ مَرُّوا عَلَى مَنْ فَوْقَهُمْ فَقَالُوا لَوْ أَنَّا خَرَقْنَا فِي نَصِيبِنَا خَرْقًا، وَلَمْ نُؤْذِ مَنْ فَوْقَنَا‏.‏ فَإِنْ يَتْرُكُوهُمْ وَمَا أَرَادُوا هَلَكُوا جَمِيعًا، وَإِنْ أَخَذُوا عَلَى أَيْدِيهِمْ نَجَوْا وَنَجَوْا جَمِيعًا ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated An-Nu`man bin Bashir:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The example of the person abiding by Allah's order and restrictions in comparison to those who violate them is like the example of those persons who drew lots for their seats in a boat. Some of them got seats in the upper part, and the others in the lower. When the latter needed water, they had to go up to bring water (and that troubled the others), so they said, 'Let us make a hole in our share of the ship (and get water) saving those who are above us from troubling them. So, if the people in the upper part left the others do what they had suggested, all the people of the ship would be destroyed, but if they prevented them, both parties would be safe

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاذُ بْنُ فَضَالَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عُمَرَ، حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْجُلُوسَ عَلَى الطُّرُقَاتِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَا لَنَا بُدٌّ، إِنَّمَا هِيَ مَجَالِسُنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ فِيهَا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِذَا أَبَيْتُمْ إِلاَّ الْمَجَالِسَ فَأَعْطُوا الطَّرِيقَ حَقَّهَا ‏"‏ قَالُوا وَمَا حَقُّ الطَّرِيقِ قَالَ ‏"‏ غَضُّ الْبَصَرِ، وَكَفُّ الأَذَى، وَرَدُّ السَّلاَمِ، وَأَمْرٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، وَنَهْىٌ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Beware! Avoid sitting on the roads (ways)." The people said, "There is no way out of it as these are our sitting places where we have talks." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If you must sit there, then observe the rights of the way." They asked, "What are the rights of the way?" He said, "They are the lowering of your gazes (on seeing what is illegal to look at), refraining from harming people, returning greetings, advocating good and forbidding evil

title: Honoured by Our Creator: Reflections on Human Dignity
summary: The Qur'an speaks of an honour given to every human being. How that dignity shapes the way we see strangers, those who differ from us and those in our care.

sections.heading: Dignity as a gift
paragraphs: Before any title, wealth or achievement, the Qur'an speaks of an honour that belongs to every human being. It tells us that the Children of Adam have been honoured, carried over land and sea, provided with good things and preferred above much of creation [Q 17:70]. This dignity is not earned by status. It is given by the One who created us.

Another verse describes the human being as created in the best of stature [Q 95:4]. Whatever we think of our own bodies, abilities or circumstances, the starting point the Qur'an offers is one of worth and care in our making.

To reflect on this is to change how we look at people. The stranger at the bus stop, the colleague we find difficult, the person whose language we do not speak: each of them carries the same honour that we hope others will see in us.

sections.heading: Difference without hierarchy
paragraphs: The Qur'an addresses all of humankind when it says that people were created male and female and made into nations and tribes so that they may know one another [Q 49:13]. Difference, in this verse, is a reason for acquaintance, not for contempt.

The same verse then names the only measure of nobility it recognises: the best in conduct, in the sight of God, who knows and is aware of all things [Q 49:13]. Lineage, colour and nationality are real parts of who we are, but they are not a ladder on which some stand above others.

This is both humbling and freeing. It is humbling because no one can claim superiority by birth. It is freeing because every person, whatever their background, has the same path to honour open before them: good conduct.

sections.heading: A lesson at a funeral
paragraphs: A short narration shows how the Prophet (peace be upon him) lived this teaching. When a funeral procession passed in front of him, he stood up. When he was told that it was the coffin of a Jewish man, he answered by asking whether it was not a living soul [H bukhari 1312].

The narration tells us that Sahl bin Hunaif and Qais bin Sa`d, sitting in Al-Qadisiya, stood up for the funeral of a non-Muslim from that land, and explained their action by recalling what they had seen from him [H bukhari 1312]. The lesson was remembered and passed on through practice.
Respect here is not tied to shared belief. It rests on a shared humanity. That simple question, about whether this was not a soul, invites us to see the person before we see the label.

sections.heading: Words that wound
paragraphs: Dignity is also protected or damaged in everyday speech. Abu Dhar, a close companion, once insulted a man by speaking badly of his mother. The Prophet told him that this showed a trace of the days of ignorance still in him [H bukhari 30].

He then reminded him that those placed under one's command are brothers, that one should feed them from what one eats and clothe them from what one wears, not burden them beyond their capacity, and help them when the work is heavy [H bukhari 30]. The narration opens with a visitor noticing that Abu Dhar and his slave were wearing the same kind of cloak, and this teaching was the reason he gave [H bukhari 30].

The social setting of that time was different from ours, but the principle carries over clearly. Power over another person, whether as an employer, a manager, a parent or a teacher, does not reduce their worth. It increases our responsibility to treat them well.

sections.heading: Carrying the lesson forward
paragraphs: Human dignity is easy to affirm in general and harder to honour in particular moments: when we are tired, when someone is different from us, or when we hold some advantage over them. These texts meet us in exactly those moments.

We might begin with small things: how we speak about people who are not present, how we treat those who serve us, and whether we let jokes about someone's origins pass. Each is a chance to remember the honour God has placed in every person [Q 17:70].
In the end, the measure that matters is conduct [Q 49:13]. That is a measure we can work on every day, with humility, asking God to help us see others as He has honoured them.

ayahs.arabic: ۞وَلَقَدۡ كَرَّمۡنَا بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَرَزَقۡنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرࣲ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَا تَفۡضِيلࣰ ا
ayahs.english: Verily we have honoured the Children of Adam. We carry them on the land and the sea, and have made provision of good things for them, and have preferred them above many of those whom We created with a marked preferment

ayahs.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
ayahs.english: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

ayahs.arabic: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمࣲ‏
ayahs.english: Surely We created man of the best stature

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مُرَّةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ أَبِي لَيْلَى، قَالَ كَانَ سَهْلُ بْنُ حُنَيْفٍ وَقَيْسُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ قَاعِدَيْنِ بِالْقَادِسِيَّةِ، فَمَرُّوا عَلَيْهِمَا بِجَنَازَةٍ فَقَامَا‏.‏ فَقِيلَ لَهُمَا إِنَّهَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الأَرْضِ، أَىْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ فَقَالاَ إِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَرَّتْ بِهِ جَنَازَةٌ فَقَامَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّهَا جَنَازَةُ يَهُودِيٍّ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ أَلَيْسَتْ نَفْسًا ‏"‏‏.‏ وَقَالَ أَبُو حَمْزَةَ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، قَالَ كُنْتُ مَعَ قَيْسٍ وَسَهْلٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ فَقَالاَ كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ وَقَالَ زَكَرِيَّاءُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى كَانَ أَبُو مَسْعُودٍ وَقَيْسٌ يَقُومَانِ لِلْجِنَازَةِ‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated `Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila:Sahl bin Hunaif and Qais bin Sa`d were sitting in the city of Al-Qadisiya. A funeral procession passed in front of them and they stood up. They were told that funeral procession was of one of the inhabitants of the land i.e. of a non-believer, under the protection of Muslims. They said, "A funeral procession passed in front of the Prophet (ﷺ) and he stood up. When he was told that it was the coffin of a Jew, he said, "Is it not a living being (soul)?

hadiths.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ وَاصِلٍ الأَحْدَبِ، عَنِ الْمَعْرُورِ، قَالَ لَقِيتُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ بِالرَّبَذَةِ، وَعَلَيْهِ حُلَّةٌ، وَعَلَى غُلاَمِهِ حُلَّةٌ، فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ إِنِّي سَابَبْتُ رَجُلاً، فَعَيَّرْتُهُ بِأُمِّهِ، فَقَالَ لِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ أَعَيَّرْتَهُ بِأُمِّهِ إِنَّكَ امْرُؤٌ فِيكَ جَاهِلِيَّةٌ، إِخْوَانُكُمْ خَوَلُكُمْ، جَعَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ تَحْتَ أَيْدِيكُمْ، فَمَنْ كَانَ أَخُوهُ تَحْتَ يَدِهِ فَلْيُطْعِمْهُ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ، وَلْيُلْبِسْهُ مِمَّا يَلْبَسُ، وَلاَ تُكَلِّفُوهُمْ مَا يَغْلِبُهُمْ، فَإِنْ كَلَّفْتُمُوهُمْ فَأَعِينُوهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏
hadiths.english: Narrated Al-Ma'rur: At Ar-Rabadha I met Abu Dhar who was wearing a cloak, and his slave, too, was wearing a similar one. I asked about the reason for it. He replied, "I abused a person by calling his mother with bad names." The Prophet said to me, 'O Abu Dhar! Did you abuse him by calling his mother with bad names You still have some characteristics of ignorance. Your slaves are your brothers and Allah has put them under your command. So whoever has a brother under his command should feed him of what he eats and dress him of what he wears. Do not ask them (slaves) to do things beyond their capacity (power) and if you do so, then help them
